Name: Location Preload - Fast Map Loading and Stutter Fix - Performance Optimization
Author: ZeroXPatch
Description:
[b]Another mod inspired by one of the functions from [/b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/28950]No More Lag[/url].

This mod was inspired by the simple idea of “preload maps before you need them,” but it’s implemented with a more flexible system and configurable behavior. Location Preload offers three GMCM-selectable modes: [b]Location Exit Preload[/b] (similar to the classic “preload all exits” approach), [b]Door Tile Preload[/b] (a more targeted, near-door preload, which is a new mode), and [b]Hybrid[/b] (a combination of the two).


[color=#ff7700][size=3]What you should know about this mod when enabling hub mode/both, if you do not want the long initial load, you can just use the nearest mode
[/size][/color][quote][color=#00ffff][size=3]On my setup, initially loading a save takes about 12 seconds without preloading. With Location Preload enabled, the game starts warming up nearby maps during the load, so my initial load time increases to about 23 seconds. But later map loading will be much smoother.

This mod doesn’t remove loading, it shifts it earlier by preloading maps ahead of time, so location transitions are smoother later.

[/size][/color][color=#00ff00]it's not magic, you will "suffer" either way :D, might as well "suffer" earlier.
[/color][/quote][center][b]
[color=#ffff00][size=6]Location Preload
[/size][/color][color=#00ff00][size=3]
[/size][/color][/b][size=3]Safe to uninstall anytime. Removing it just disables the features.

[/size][size=3][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/ZeroXPatch/mods?gameId=1303&sortBy=endorsements]https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/ZeroXPatch/mods?gameId=1303&sortBy=endorsements[/url][/size][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/ZeroXPatch/mods?gameId=1303&sortBy=downloads]
[/url][/center][b]Location Preload[/b] reduces stutter when moving between areas by [b]preloading map assets in advance[/b]. 

Instead of the game loading a big map file [i]right as you enter a door/exit[/i] (which can cause a hitch), this mod warms the cache gradually while you’re already playing.

It’s designed to be lightweight and configurable, with options to preload [b]all exits from a location[/b], [b]only the door you’re approaching[/b], or [b]both[/b].
[line][b][color=#00ff00]What this mod helps with
[/color][/b]
Stardew can pause briefly when it needs to load a location for the first time (especially with large modded maps like SVE / East Scarp / expanded interiors). Location

Preload helps by:
[list]
[*][b]Smoother door transitions[/b] (entering shops, houses, interiors)
[*][b]Less stutter on map-edge exits[/b] (Town ↔ Bus Stop, Forest ↔ Farm, etc.)
[*][b]Better performance in big modded hubs[/b] where moving around triggers lots of first-time loads
[/list]This won’t eliminate every possible hitch (NPC pathing, events, multiplayer sync, etc. can still cause spikes), but it [b]reduces the “first-time location load” cost[/b], which is one of the most common causes of transition stutter.
[line][b][color=#00ff00]How it works
[/color][/b]
[b][color=#ffff00]when enabling hub mode or both, if you do not want the long initial load, you can just use the nearest mode

[/color][/b]1) [b][color=#ffff00]Initial save load may take longer[/color][/b] (and why)When you load into a save, the game normally only loads what it immediately needs. With Location Preload enabled, you may notice that the [b][color=#ffff00]first 10–30 seconds[/color][/b] after entering the world can be a bit heavier, because the mod starts preloading maps [i]in the background[/i] (spread across ticks).
[b]
Why this happens:[/b]
The mod intentionally does the “expensive first load” earlier—while you’re just walking around or standing still—so you don’t get that same cost later when you hit a door or exit.

[b]What gets preloaded at this stage:[/b]
Right after you appear in the world and start moving around, Location Preload will queue maps based on your current configuration:

[list]
[*][b]Hub mode:[/b] preloads the locations you can reach from your current location’s exits/doors (warp targets).
Example: If you enter [b]Town[/b], it may queue maps like [b]Bus Stop[/b], [b]Forest[/b], [b]Backwoods[/b], etc. (plus modded exits if they’re in the warp list).[*][b]Nearest mode:[/b] preloads only the [b]closest exit(s)[/b] near you as you walk around.
[*][b]Both:[/b] does Hub preloads + Nearest “just in time” preloads.
[/list]Because this is real map loading (not fake), it can make the start of a session feel slightly heavier—[b]but the payoff is fewer stutters later[/b].
[line][color=#00ffff]2) Later warps and doors (during normal gameplay)
[/color]
After that initial warm-up, the mod keeps helping as you play:

Hub mode (after you arrive somewhere)Each time you warp into a location, the mod looks at that location’s exits and doors and [b]queues the target maps[/b].

This gives the mod time to preload while you move around inside the area.

Nearest mode (before you enter a door/exit)While you walk, the mod periodically checks which exit/door warp is closest (and optionally the one you’re facing) and preloads [b]only that map[/b].

This is great for:

[list]
[*]Large modded maps
[*]Players who don’t want to preload “everything”
[*]Minimizing background work
[/list]Both mode

Combines both strategies:

[list]
[*]Hub mode gives you broad coverage in hubs (Town, Forest, etc.)
[*]Nearest mode tops it up for the door you’re actually walking toward
[/list][line][color=#00ffff]3) “Reloading exits” and why it keeps working
[/color]
Location Preload remembers what it already preloaded (for the current play session/day), so it doesn’t constantly reload the same maps over and over. When you:
[list]
[*]return to a hub (like Town),
[*]re-enter a shop,
[*]or bounce between two areas,
[/list]…those maps are often already warmed up, so transitions tend to stay smoother.

There’s also a config option [b]“Clear queue on warp”[/b]:

[list]
[*][b]On:[/b] clears [i]pending[/i] preloads whenever you change locations (keeps behavior predictable)
[*][b]Off:[/b] keeps queued items (more aggressive preloading)
[/list]Already preloaded maps are still tracked so the mod avoids redundant work.

[line][b][color=#00ff00]Configuration (GMCM supported)
[/color][/b]
If you have [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b], you can configure everything in-game:
[list]
[*][b]Preload Mode:[/b] Hub / Nearest / Both
[*][b]Nearest tuning:[/b] how many exits to preload, max distance, scan interval, prefer the door you’re facing
[*][b]Performance limits:[/b] max maps per tick, max milliseconds per tick
[*][b]Optional custom location list:[/b] always preload specific locations you care about
[/list][line][b][color=#00ff00]Tips

[/color][/b][list]
[*]For big modded installs, start with:
[list]
[*][b]Mode: Both[/b]
[*][b]Max maps per tick: 1[/b]
[*][b]Max ms per tick: 2–3[/b]
[/list][*]If you feel the game is “busy” right after loading a save, lower:
[list]
[*]Max maps per tick
[*]Max ms per tick
[*]or switch to [b]Nearest[/b] mode
[/list][/list]

[b][color=#ffff00][size=6][center]F&Q[/center][/size][/color][/b][b]FAQ / Troubleshooting (Location Preload)
[/b]
[b][color=#ffff00]Does Location Preload work with Stardew Valley Expanded / East Scarp / other big mods?
[/color][/b]
Yes. Location Preload preloads [b]map assets[/b] through SMAPI’s content system, which works fine with Content Patcher and big expansions. If you’re using lots of large maps, this mod can help reduce the “first time entering today” stutter.

[line][b][color=#ffff00]Why does loading my save take longer?
[/color][/b]
Because the mod starts [b]preloading maps early[/b] (spread across ticks) so the game doesn’t have to do that heavy work right when you hit a door/exit later.

Think of it like this:
[list]
[*][b]Without[/b] this mod: the “cost” happens when you enter a door → hitch during transition.
[*][b]With[/b] this mod: some of that cost happens shortly after loading the save → smoother transitions later.
[/list]If you don’t like the heavier warm-up period, reduce:

[list]
[*][b]Max maps per tick[/b]
[*][b]Max ms per tick[/b]
[*]or switch [b]Mode[/b] to [b]Nearest[/b].
[/list][line][b][color=#ffff00]What maps are being preloaded?
[/color][/b]
Depends on your mode/settings:

[b]Hub mode[/b]
[list]
[*]After you warp into a location, the mod queues the maps you can reach from there (doors/exits).
[*]Example: entering [b]Town[/b] may queue maps like [b]BusStop[/b], [b]Forest[/b], etc. (plus modded targets if present).
[/list][b]Nearest mode[/b]
[list]
[*]While you walk around, the mod queues only the [b]closest exit(s)[/b] (and optionally the one you’re facing).
[/list][b]Both[/b]
[list]
[*]Hub coverage + Nearest “just in time” top-ups.
[/list][line][b][color=#ffff00]Does this remove [i]all[/i] lag when entering buildings/areas?
[/color][/b]
No. It reduces [b]map asset loading stutter[/b], but other things can still cause lag:

[list]
[*]NPC updates/pathfinding
[*]events/scripts running
[*]multiplayer syncing
[*]very heavy tilesheets/textures on first use
[/list]It helps most with the “loading map for the first time” part.
[line][b][color=#ffff00]I see lots of lines like “Preloaded map: Maps/Town” in my SMAPI console
[/color][/b]
That’s normal if [b]Verbose logging[/b] is enabled. Turn it off in GMCM if you don’t want the spam.
[line][b][color=#ffff00]Is it safe? Will it corrupt my save?
[/color][/b]
It does not edit saves or game data. It only [b]loads assets earlier[/b]. Worst case, if an asset fails to load, it will log the error and continue.
[line][b][color=#ffff00]Will this increase RAM usage?
[/color][/b]
Potentially a bit, yes. Preloading keeps more assets warm in memory/cache, which can increase memory use. If you’re tight on RAM, use:

[list]
[*][b]Nearest[/b] mode,
[*]a smaller [b]max distance[/b],
[*]and lower [b]per-tick budgets[/b].
[/list][line][b][color=#ffff00]I’m getting stutter [/color][/b][i][b][color=#ffff00]because of this mod
[/color][/b]
[/i]If you preload too aggressively, you can create “micro-stutters” while walking.Fix by lowering:
[list]
[*][b]Max maps per tick[/b]
[*][b]Max ms per tick[/b]
[*]increase [b]Nearest check interval[/b]
[*]reduce [b]Nearest warp count[/b]
[*]reduce [b]Nearest max distance[/b]
Or switch to [b]Nearest[/b] only.[/list][line][b][color=#ffff00]Does it work in multiplayer?
[/color][/b]
Yes, it should. It runs client-side and just preloads content. However, multiplayer can still have hitching due to network/state sync unrelated to map loading.
[line][b][color=#ffff00]Does it conflict with Content Patcher?
[/color][/b]
No conflict normally. Location Preload requests map assets through SMAPI the same way the game does. Content Patcher can still apply replacements/edits.

If you ever see Content Patcher errors, they’re usually caused by the content pack itself (bad asset type, missing file, etc.).

The only difference is: preloading may cause those assets to be requested earlier, so errors show up sooner.
[line][b][color=#ffff00]Best settings for big modpacks (recommended starting point)
[/color][/b]
[list]
[*][b]Mode:[/b] Both
[*][b]Max maps per tick:[/b] 1
[*][b]Max ms per tick:[/b] 2–3
[*][b]Nearest max distance:[/b] 6–10
[*][b]Nearest check interval:[/b] 6–10 ticks
[*][b]Nearest warp count:[/b] 1
[/list]Then adjust based on how it feels.
